title: Wie, wat, waar?
subtitle: Asking questions
intro: In this lesson you will learn the main Dutch question words and how to build simple open questions. You can ask where someone lives, where they are from, why they study Dutch, and which question or answer they mean. You will also practise a short class interview.

example.en: How much coffee do you want?

words.note: Use welke before de-words and plural nouns.
After omdat the verb goes at the end.

words.forms: ik vraag, jij vraagt, wij vragen
words.note: As a noun, de vraag has plural vragen.

words.forms: ik antwoord, jij antwoordt, wij antwoorden
words.note: As a noun, het antwoord has plural antwoorden.

words.forms: ik weet, jij weet, wij weten
ik ken, jij kent, wij kennen
words.note: Use kennen for people and places.

example.en: Of course, I have the answer.

example.nl: In de klas spreken we Nederlands.

words.note: Waar and vandaan go around the verb and subject.

phrases.note: Waar and vandaan split around the verb and subject.
Fixed chunk: the verb goes at the end after omdat.

grammar.title: Question words
grammar.explanation: Use a question word to ask for open information. The question word comes first, then the verb, then the subject: **Waar woon je?** **Waarom studeer je Nederlands?** For **waar ... vandaan**, the word **vandaan** goes at the end: **Waar kom je vandaan?**
grammar.tip: Learn the question words as a set: wie, wat, waar, wanneer, hoe, waarom, hoeveel, welk, welke.

grammar.title: Open questions: question word + verb + subject
grammar.explanation: In an open question the first word is the question word. Then comes the verb, then the subject: **Waar woon je?** **Wanneer is de presentatie?** With **jij/je** after the verb, the verb has no extra **-t**: **Waar woon je?**

examples.en: How many questions do you have?

grammar.tip: In a simple open question, the verb is the second element.

grammar.title: welk or welke?
grammar.explanation: **Welk** goes with het-words: **welk nummer**, **welk antwoord**. **Welke** goes with de-words and plurals: **welke vraag**, **welke dag**, **welke vragen**. If you know the article, you know the form.
grammar.tip: het -> welk; de or plural -> welke.

dialogue.title: Een interview in de klas
dialogue.setting: In class, Sanne interviews her classmate Daan for a short presentation about him.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Hoi Daan, ik heb een vraag.
lines.en: Hi Daan, I have a question.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.en: Because I live in the Netherlands.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Dank je wel! Dat is een goed interview.
lines.en: Thank you! That is a good interview.

exercises.prompt: You want to know where someone lives. Choose the question word.
exercises.explain: Use 'Waar' for a place: 'Waar woon je?'

exercises.prompt: You want to ask someone's name. Choose the question word.
exercises.explain: Use 'Hoe' to ask a name: 'Hoe heet je?'
'Het antwoord' is a het-word, so use 'welk': 'Welk antwoord is goed?'

exercises.prompt: You want to ask the price. Choose the question word.
exercises.explain: 'Hoeveel' asks about an amount or price: 'Hoeveel kost het?'
In an open question, the question word comes first, then the verb, then the subject. With 'je' after the verb, 'woon' has no -t: 'Waar woon je?'
'Het antwoord' is a het-word, so use 'het'. The verb 'is' comes after the subject: 'Het antwoord is goed.'
The question word comes first, then the verb 'is', then the subject: 'Wanneer is de presentatie?'
Use 'Waar' for a place: 'Waar woon je?'
Dutch asks for a name with 'Hoe heet je?' (literally: how are you called?).
Use 'kennen' for people and places. After 'ik' the form is 'ken': 'Ik ken de leraar.'

mistakes.pattern: Puts the verb before the question word (Woon waar je?)
mistakes.explain: Start with the question word: 'Waar woon je?'

mistakes.pattern: Adds -t after je (Waar woont je?)
mistakes.explain: With 'je' after the verb, the verb has no -t: 'Waar woon je?'

mistakes.pattern: Leaves out the question word (Woon je?)
mistakes.explain: An open question starts with a question word: 'Waar woon je?'

mistakes.pattern: Puts the subject before the verb (Waarom je studeert Nederlands?)
mistakes.explain: After the question word comes the verb, then the subject: 'Waarom studeer je Nederlands?'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'omdat' in the question (Omdat studeer je Nederlands?)
mistakes.explain: Use 'waarom' to ask why: 'Waarom studeer je Nederlands?'

mistakes.pattern: Adds -t after je (Waarom studeert je Nederlands?)
mistakes.explain: With 'je' after the verb, the verb has no -t: 'Waarom studeer je Nederlands?'

mistakes.pattern: Puts 'Nederlands' before the verb (Waarom Nederlands studeer je?)
mistakes.explain: The verb comes second: 'Waarom studeer je Nederlands?'

mistakes.pattern: Puts the verb at the end (Ik het antwoord weet.)
mistakes.explain: The verb comes second: 'Ik weet het antwoord.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'heb' instead of 'weet' (Ik heb het antwoord.)
mistakes.explain: Use 'weten' for knowing a fact: 'Ik weet het antwoord.' ('Ik heb het antwoord' means I have the answer.)

mistakes.pattern: Forgets 'het' (Ik weet antwoord.)
mistakes.explain: Use 'het antwoord': 'Ik weet het antwoord.'

mistakes.pattern: Adds -t after ik (Ik weett het antwoord.)
mistakes.explain: After 'ik' the form is 'weet', with no extra -t: 'Ik weet het antwoord.'

exercises.context: You are in class. Your teacher asks: 'Heb je een vraag?'
exercises.task: Say yes, you have a question.
examples: Ja, natuurlijk. Ik heb een vraag.

mistakes.pattern: Answers no instead of yes (Nee, ik heb geen vraag.)
mistakes.explain: The task asks you to say yes: 'Ja, ik heb een vraag.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'ben' instead of 'heb' (Ja, ik ben een vraag.)
mistakes.explain: Use 'hebben' for having a question: 'Ik heb een vraag.'

mistakes.pattern: Leaves out 'een' (Ja, ik heb vraag.)
mistakes.explain: Use 'een' before 'vraag': 'Ik heb een vraag.'

exercises.context: Your classmate asks: 'Waarom studeer je Nederlands?'
exercises.task: Give a simple reason: you live in the Netherlands.

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'waarom' instead of 'omdat' (Waarom ik woon in Nederland.)
mistakes.explain: Use 'omdat' to give a reason: 'Omdat ik in Nederland woon.'

mistakes.pattern: Puts the verb before the end after omdat (Omdat ik woon in Nederland.)
mistakes.explain: After 'omdat' the verb goes at the end: 'Omdat ik in Nederland woon.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'ben' instead of 'woon' (Omdat ik in Nederland ben.)
mistakes.explain: Use 'wonen' for living: 'Omdat ik in Nederland woon.'

mistakes.pattern: Forgets 'in' (Omdat ik Nederland woon.)
mistakes.explain: Use 'in' before the country: 'Omdat ik in Nederland woon.'

roleplay.title: Interview je klasgenoot
roleplay.setting: In class, you interview your classmate Daan for a short presentation about him.

turns.task: Greet Daan and say you have a question.
examples: Hoi Daan, ik heb een vraag.

mistakes.pattern: Skips the greeting and only says 'Ik heb een vraag.'
mistakes.explain: Start with a greeting: 'Hoi Daan, ik heb een vraag.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'ben' instead of 'heb' (Ik ben een vraag.)
mistakes.explain: Use 'hebben' for having a question: 'Ik heb een vraag.'

mistakes.pattern: Leaves out 'een' (Ik heb vraag.)
mistakes.explain: Use 'een' before 'vraag': 'Ik heb een vraag.'

mistakes.pattern: Puts the verb before the question word (Woon waar je?)
mistakes.explain: Start with the question word: 'Waar woon je?'

mistakes.pattern: Adds -t after je (Waar woont je?)
mistakes.explain: With 'je' after the verb, the verb has no -t: 'Waar woon je?'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'is' instead of 'woon' (Waar is je?)
mistakes.explain: Use 'wonen' for where you live: 'Waar woon je?'

mistakes.pattern: Leaves out 'vandaan' (Waar kom je?)
mistakes.explain: 'Where are you from?' is 'Waar kom je vandaan?'

mistakes.pattern: Puts 'vandaan' before the verb (Waar vandaan kom je?)
mistakes.explain: Put 'vandaan' at the end: 'Waar kom je vandaan?'

mistakes.pattern: Adds -t after je (Waar komt je vandaan?)
mistakes.explain: With 'je' after the verb, the verb has no -t: 'Waar kom je vandaan?'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'omdat' in the question (Omdat studeer je Nederlands?)
mistakes.explain: Use 'waarom' to ask why: 'Waarom studeer je Nederlands?'

mistakes.pattern: Puts the subject before the verb (Waarom je studeert Nederlands?)
mistakes.explain: Question word + verb + subject: 'Waarom studeer je Nederlands?'

mistakes.pattern: Adds -t after je (Waarom studeert je Nederlands?)
mistakes.explain: With 'je' after the verb, the verb has no -t: 'Waarom studeer je Nederlands?'

say.en: Because I live in the Netherlands.

turns.task: Thank him and say the presentation is tomorrow.
examples: Dank je wel! De presentatie is morgen.
Dank je! De presentatie is morgen.

mistakes.pattern: Forgets to thank (De presentatie is morgen.)
mistakes.explain: Start with 'Dank je wel' or 'Dank je'.

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'ben' instead of 'is' (De presentatie ben morgen.)
mistakes.explain: Use 'is' with 'de presentatie': 'De presentatie is morgen.'

mistakes.pattern: Puts 'morgen' before 'is' (De presentatie morgen is.)
mistakes.explain: The verb comes second: 'De presentatie is morgen.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'het presentatie' (Het presentatie is morgen.)
mistakes.explain: 'Presentatie' is a de-word: 'de presentatie'.

culture.title: Direct questions are normal
culture.text: In the Netherlands, people often ask several short questions in a row: where do you live, where are you from, what do you do? This is usually friendly interest, not a police interview. A short answer is normal, and you can ask the same question back. Dutch directness can feel rude to some learners, but it is rarely meant that way.

summary: Use question words like wie, wat, waar, wanneer, hoe, waarom, hoeveel, welk and welke.
Open questions start with question word + verb + subject: Waar woon je?
Use welk with het-words and welke with de-words and plurals.
Use weten for facts and kennen for people and places.
Use omdat to give a reason; the verb goes at the end: Omdat ik in Utrecht woon.
